εἰ δὲ τοῦτο ἀληθές ἐστιν, κατὰ τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς ἐρῶ· ἄρα οὐκ ἦν οὐδ' ἔσται ἐν βίῳ τὸ καλόν, οὔτε τίς ποτ' αὐτὸ ἐνήργησεν, εἴγε κατ' ἀναίρεσιν τοῦ καλοῦ καὶ ἀγαθοῦ ἐπὶ παντὸς ἀνθρώπου ἐκλαμβάνωσιν, ὅτι ὃ θέλω ἀγαθόν, τοῦτο οὐ ποιῶ, ἀλλ' ὃ μισῶ τοῦτο
πράσσω. πόθεν δὲ καὶ ἐν τῷ τῶν ἀνθρώπων βίῳ 5 ἀρετῶν ὀνόματα εὑρέθη; εἰ δέ εἰσιν ἐνεργοῦντες τὸ καλόν, κἂν ὀλίγοι εἶεν οἱ τοῦτο δρῶντες, ἄρ' οὐχ οἱ πάντες φήσουσιν· οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι οὐκ οἰκεῖ ἐν ἡμῖν ἀγαθόν· ὃ γὰρ ἠθέλησαν ἀγαθόν, τοῦτο πράττουσιν. εἰ δὲ οἱ τὸ ἀγαθὸν ἐνεργοῦντες ἐν σαρκὶ ὑπάρχοντες τοῦτο ἐνεργοῦσιν, καὶ οἱ τοῦτο μὴ ποιοῦντες ἀλλὰ τὸ κακὸν ἐν σαρκί εἰσίν, ἄρ' οὐ τῇ σαρκὶ τὸ αἴτιον τοῦ μὴ γίνεσθαι τὸ ἀγαθὸν περιαπτέον, ἀλλὰ τῇ τούτων μαλακοψυχίᾳ. εἰ γὰρ τοῖς ἐθέλουσι τὸ καλὸν ποιῆσαι παροικεῖται τὸ κακόν, ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ τοῖς ἐθέλουσι κακοεργεῖν οὐ καλὸν παράκειται, προνοήσαντες δὲ καὶ προθελήσαντες ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον ἐνεργείας ἔρχονται, ἄρ' οὐ φύσει καὶ οὐσίᾳ τὰ σώματα ἡμῶν ἐστι φαῦλα· τῶν γὰρ πρακτέων ἡμῶν προηγεῖται βουλὴ καὶ θέλησις, ψυχῆς δὲ ταῦτα φρόνημα ἐχούσης αὐτεξούσιον, ῥέψαι δυναμένης πρὸς ἃς βούλεται πράξεις. Νυνὶ δὲ οὐκέτι ἐγὼ κατεργάζομαι αὐτό, ἀλλ' ἡ οἰκοῦσα ἐν ἐμοὶ ἁμαρτία. ἀπελογήσατο διὰ τούτου τοῦ λογίου, ὅτι περ οὐ φαύλη κατὰ φύσιν ἡ σάρξ· οὐ γὰρ ἡ σὰρξ ἣν περικείμεθα οἰκεῖ ἐν ἡμῖν, ἀλλ' ὁ ἐν τοῖς παρανόμοις οἰκῶν διάβολος. ᾧ γὰρ λέγω· Χριστὸς οἰκεῖ ἐν παντὶ δικαίῳ τὸ ἀγαθὸν ἐργαζομένῳ, τὸν αὐτὸν οἶμαι τρόπον οἰκεῖν τὸν διάβολον ἐν παντὶ κακοποιῷ. οὐκοῦν οὐχ ἡμεῖς ἐσμεν καθὸ σάρκα ἔχομεν πονηροί, ἀλλ' ἡ οἰκοῦσα ἐν ἡμῖν ἁμαρτία, ἄλλη τις οὖσα παρὰ τὴν σάρκα καὶ τὴν ψυχὴν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου· καὶ γὰρ ἐν ψυχῇ μάλιστα λέγεται ἐπιχωριάζειν ὁ διάβολος κατὰ τὸ εἰσῆλθεν ὁ σατανᾶς εἰς τὴν καρδίαν Ἰούδα, καὶ κατὰ τὸ Ἀνανία, ἵνα τί ἐπλήρωσεν ὁ σατανᾶς τὴν καρδίαν σου; εὖ δὲ καὶ τὸ εἰπεῖν οὐκέτι ἐγὼ κατεργάζομαι αὐτὸ ἀλλ' ἡ οἰκοῦσα ἐν ἐμοὶ ἁμαρτία· ἔργου γὰρ καὶ κατέργου πολὺ τὸ μέσον, διότι τοῦ ἔργου προηγεῖται τὸ κάτεργον ὡς φέρε εἰπεῖν οἰκίας ἢ νηός· τὸ δὲ κάτεργον, τοῦτ' ἔστι τῆς ὕλης ἡ προπαρασκευή. ἡ τοίνυν οἰκοῦσα ἐν τοῖς ἁμαρτάνουσιν ἁμαρτία, τοῦτ' ἔστιν ὁ σατανᾶς, ὁμολογουμένως ἐν τοῖς λογισμοῖς ἡμῶν προκατεργάζεται τοῦ ἐσομένου κακοῦ τῆς ἰδέας, τὴν κατασκευήν, τῆς ὑποδεξαμένης αὐτὸν ψυχῆς συμπραττούσης αὐτῷ τῆς κακίας καθάπερ τοῖς σπείρουσιν ἡ τῆς θήλεος μήτρα πρὸς τὸ 3 τελεσφορηθῆναι τὸ σπαρέν. καὶ ἐπειδήπερ ἐκ τῆς καρδίας ἐκπορεύονται λογισμοὶ πονηροί, ἐκ τῆς γενομένης τοῦ διαβόλου συλλήψεως, κέκραγε τὸ θεῖον λόγιον· λογισμοὺς καθαιροῦντες καὶ πᾶν ὕψωμα ἐπαιρόμενον κατὰ τῆς γνώσεως τοῦ θεοῦ. ὥσπερ τοίνυν ταῖς φιλαρέτοις ψυχαῖς τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα συγκοπιᾶν λέγεται κατὰ τὸ περισσότερον πάντων ἐκοπίασα, οὐκ ἐγὼ δὲ ἀλλ' ἡ χάρις τοῦ θεοῦ ἡ σὺν ἐμοί, οὕτω δὴ ἐπὰν ῥᾴθυμος ψυχὴ ταῖς 6 τοῦ διαβόλου προτροπαῖς πεισθῇ, συνεργὸν ἔχει πρὸς τὸ κακὸν αὐτὸν τὸν διάβολον· αὐτὸς γὰρ καὶ τὸν τύπον τῆς ἐσομένης ἁμαρτίας προκατειργάσατο ἐν αὐτῇ. ὅτου χάριν εἴρηται οὐκέτι ἐγὼ κατεργάζομαι αὐτό, ἀλλ' ἡ οἰκοῦσα ἐν ἐμοὶ ἁμαρτία. 4
thought_title: The devil, not the flesh, works sin in us
orientation: Didymus is answering an impious objection to Paul's words in Romans 7:18-19, arguing that if no one can do the good they will, then virtue would be impossible, and he now explains that the indwelling sin is the devil, not the flesh.
pass_a_gloss: But if this is true, I will speak according to the impious: then the good was not and will not be in life, nor did anyone ever work it, if indeed they take it as the abolition of the good and beautiful upon every human being, that what I will as good, this I do not do, but what I hate, this I practice. And from where also in the life of humans were names of virtues found? But if there are those working the good, even if few might be those doing this, then will not all say: but we know that good does not dwell in us; for what they willed as good, this they practice. But if those working the good while being in flesh work this, and those not doing this but the evil are in flesh, then is not the cause of the good not coming about to be attached to the flesh, but to the moral weakness of soul of these? For if to those willing to do the good the evil dwells beside, and likewise also to those willing to do evil the good lies beside, and having purposed beforehand and willed beforehand they come to so much of activity, then are not our bodies by nature and substance worthless? For of our deeds the counsel and willing go before, and these are the thought of a soul having free will, able to incline toward whatever actions it wishes. But now no longer do I work it out, but the sin dwelling in me. He made a defense through this saying, that the flesh is not worthless by nature; for it is not the flesh which we wear around that dwells in us, but the devil dwelling in the lawless. For in the way I say: Christ dwells in every just person working the good, in the same way I think the devil dwells in every evildoer. Therefore we are not evil insofar as we have flesh, but the sin dwelling in us, being something other than the flesh and the soul of the human being; for also in the soul especially the devil is said to reside, according to the saying Satan entered into the heart of Judas, and according to the saying Ananias, why did Satan fill your heart? And well also is the saying no longer do I work it out but the sin dwelling in me; for between a work and a working-out there is much middle ground, because before the work goes the working-out, as for example of a house or a ship; and the working-out, that is the preparatory preparation of the material. The sin therefore dwelling in those who sin, that is Satan, admittedly in our reasonings works out beforehand the preparation of the idea of the coming evil, the soul that received him cooperating with him in the evil just as with those sowing the womb of the female cooperates for the sown seed to be brought to completion. And since from the heart go out evil reasonings, from the conception of the devil that has happened, the divine saying cries out: destroying reasonings and every height lifted up against the knowledge of God. Just as therefore with virtue-loving souls the Holy Spirit is said to labor together, according to the saying I labored more abundantly than all, but not I but the grace of God with me, so indeed whenever a careless soul is persuaded by the promptings of the devil, it has the devil himself as a coworker toward the evil; for he himself also worked out beforehand in it the type of the coming sin. For which reason it has been said no longer do I work it out, but the sin dwelling in me.

lemmas.gloss: softness of soul, weakness of will
to work out, bring to completion
to reside, be at home in
to bring to completion, bring to maturity

choices.why: The compound means literally softness of soul, and Didymus contrasts it with the flesh as the true cause of not doing good; keeping the literal compound preserves his point that the soul's weakness, not the body, is responsible.

The glossary requires 'work out' for κατεργάζεσθαι, and Didymus explicitly distinguishes ἔργον (work) from κάτεργον (working-out) as the preparatory stage, so the rendering must preserve the 'out' prefix.
The glossary requires 'dwell' for οἰκεῖν, and Didymus's whole argument turns on the indwelling sin being the devil, a distinct agent dwelling in the person, so 'dwelling' must be kept literal.
This compound of κατεργάζομαι with προ- is central to Didymus's distinction between the devil's preparatory working-out and the completed act; the 'beforehand' prefix must be explicit.
Didymus extends the sowing/womb metaphor from the previous clause, so 'conception' preserves the biological image of the devil's seed being received by the soul.
The glossary defines αὐτεξούσιον as the soul's power of self-determination able to incline toward actions; 'incline' captures the literal tipping motion of ῥέπω.

pass_b_english: But if this is true, I will now speak in the voice of the impious. From the impious person's perspective, the good never was and never will be in life, nor did anyone ever accomplish it, if they take the words "the good I will, this I do not do; but what I hate, this I practice" (Romans 7:19) as the abolition of the good and beautiful for every human being. And from where did the names of virtues ever appear in human life? But if there are those who enact the good, even if only a few do it, will not all of them say, "We know that good does not dwell in us"? For the good they willed, this they practice. If those who enact the good do so while existing in flesh, and those who do not do this but do evil are also in flesh, then the cause of the good not coming about must not be attached to the flesh, but to the weakness of these people's souls. For if evil dwells beside those who will to do the good, and likewise the good lies beside those who will to do evil, and after foreseeing and willing beforehand they come to such a degree of action, then our bodies are not weak by nature or substance. For deliberation and willing lead the way before our actions, and these belong to a soul that has free will, able to incline toward whatever actions it chooses.

"But now it is no longer I who do it, but the sin dwelling in me" (Romans 7:17). Through this saying he has defended the point that the flesh is not evil by nature. For it is not the flesh we are clothed in that dwells in us, but the devil who dwells in the lawless. For just as I say that Christ dwells in every righteous person who works the good, in the same way I think the devil dwells in every evildoer. Therefore we are not evil insofar as we have flesh, but the sin dwelling in us is, and it is something other than the flesh and the soul of the human being. For the devil is said to dwell especially in the soul, according to "Satan entered into Judas" (John 13:27), and according to "Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart?" (Acts 5:3).

It was well said too: "no longer I work it out, but the sin dwelling in me." For there is a great distance between a work and a working-out, because the preparation precedes the finished work, as, for example, of a house or a ship. The working-out is the prior preparation of the material. So the sin dwelling in those who sin, that is, Satan, admittedly works out beforehand in our reasonings the form of the evil to come, the construction, while the soul that has received him cooperates with him in the evil, just as the womb of the female cooperates with those who sow, so that what is sown may be brought to completion. And since evil reasonings come forth from the heart, from the conception of the devil that has taken place, the divine saying cries out: "we destroy arguments and every lofty opinion raised against the knowledge of God" (2 Corinthians 10:5). Just as the Holy Spirit is said to labor together with virtue-loving souls, according to "I labored more abundantly than all of them, yet not I, but the grace of God that is with me" (1 Corinthians 15:10), so when a careless soul is persuaded by the devil's urgings, it has the devil himself as a coworker toward evil. For he himself has worked out beforehand in it the pattern of the sin to come. For this reason it is said: "no longer I work it out, but the sin dwelling in me" (Romans 7:17).

problems.why: παροικεῖται means 'dwells beside' or 'resides near', not 'camps' which implies temporary military encampment; also 'lies beside' for παράκειται is weak.
problems.ruling: παροικεῖται = dwells beside; “camps beside” adds military sense, changing meaning.

problems.why: The English has 'its construction' but omits the preceding phrase τῆς ἰδέας ('the form/idea'); the Greek has three objects: 'the form, the construction'.
problems.ruling: Greek includes τῆς ἰδέας before τὴν κατασκευήν; omission loses a component of meaning.

problems.why: ἐνήργησεν means 'worked', 'effected', 'produced'; 'enact' suggests performing a law or drama, which is misleading for the good/virtue.
problems.ruling: ἐνήργησεν = worked/produced; “enact” misleads toward legal drama.

problems.why: Repeated: παροικεῖται is middle/passive 'dwells beside', not 'camps'.
problems.ruling: Duplicate of 1: same error with “camps beside”.

problems.why: προνοήσαντες means 'foreseeing' or 'providing for', not 'deliberating'; προθελήσαντες means 'willing beforehand'. 'After deliberating' mistranslates the first participle.
problems.ruling: προνοήσαντες = foreseeing/providing, not “deliberating”; mis‑translation changes nuance.

problems.quote: "evil reasonings come forth from the heart (Matthew 15:19)"

problems.why: The English cites Matthew 15:19, which does not appear in the Greek source.
problems.fix: Remove the parenthetical "(Matthew 15:19)" and render the passage without that citation.
problems.ruling: Matthew 15:19 is absent from Greek; source has no scripture citation at that point.

Changed 'camps beside' to 'dwells beside' for παροικεῖται, which means 'dwells beside' or 'resides near', not 'camps'.

problems.quote: the softness of soul of these people
problems.why: 'Softness' (malakia) is technical term for moral weakness/cowardice; modern reader may think physical softness.
problems.fix: Gloss as 'moral weakness' or 'lack of resolve.'

problems.quote: the womb of the female cooperates with those who sow
problems.why: Analogy is biologically crude and potentially distracting; may not capture Didymus's intent about cooperative causation.
problems.fix: Note: ancient medical analogy for cooperative causation.

problems.quote: destroying reasonings and every high thing lifted up against the knowledge of God
problems.why: 2 Corinthians 10:5 in standard Bibles reads 'we destroy arguments and every lofty opinion raised against the knowledge of God'; 'reasonings' is closer to Greek logismous but 'destroying' without 'we' alters grammar.
problems.fix: Note variant translation or supply 'we are destroying.'

problems.quote: the cause of the good not coming about must not be attached to the flesh, but to the softness of soul
problems.why: 'Softness' is an odd rendering; context needs moral weakness or laxity, not softness.
problems.fix: Use 'weakness of soul' or 'laxity of soul' instead of 'softness.'

variants.text: dwells beside those who will to do the good
the devil who dwells in the lawless

notes.why: 'Dwell' and 'reside' used interchangeably for the devil's indwelling without signaling synonymy.
notes.fix: Use 'dwell' consistently, or note 'reside' = 'dwell' on first use.
